title: Marketplace Technical Onboarding Workbook
body:
Purpose and audience:
This workbook is a pragmatic, engineering-friendly guide for taking Redwood Inference from product readiness to live listing in a cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP). Audience: GTM engineering, partner ops, partner PMs, and the solutions team that supports integration QA.

How to use this file:
- Use as the canonical pre-launch checklist for marketplace technical sign-off.
- Copy the small sections (copy snippets, SKU patterns) into partner-tailored checklists.
- Track unresolved items in the Action Items section at the bottom.

1) Integration matrix (operator view) - one-line rows you can copy into a spreadsheet:
- Asset: Listing tile + small logo (SVG/PNG). Owner: GTM design. Required: yes. Notes: provide 600x600 square, transparent background, 72ppi export.
- Asset: 3 screenshots / 2 short GIFs. Owner: Solutions eng + PM. Required: recommended. Notes: show latency dashboard, console onboarding, API example.
- Asset: 1 short video (30s). Owner: Demand gen. Required: optional. Notes: caption and hosted URL.
- Asset: Detailed tech spec PDF. Owner: Product. Required: yes. Notes: architecture diagram, network flows, ports, region availability.
- Integration: Service principal / IAM role. Owner: Partner infra. Required: yes (for provisioning tests). Notes: least-privilege role with read/write to subscription and ability to create resources (list exact perms below).
- Integration: Billing test account & SKU mapping. Owner: Finance ops. Required: yes. Notes: provide test charges + invoice sample.
- Integration: Support contact + SLA summary. Owner: Customer success. Required: yes.

2) Operator's runbook (step-by-step)
- Pre-reqs: Confirm Product PRD + versioned model id, packaging (hosted vs dedicated), and target regions.
- Step A: Register marketplace listing stub in partner portal (enter title, short desc, logo).
- Step B: Upload technical spec and provide network diagram PDF. In PDF header add: "Redwood Inference — Marketplace technical spec — v{version}".
- Step C: Create test tenancy or partner sandbox with credentials. Share service principal and ephemeral keys with QA (rotate after tests).
- Step D: Run provisioning smoke tests: API key auth, sample text generation (latency < 250ms P50 on test SKU), embeddings job (1k vectors/second target), and billing event emission. Capture traces.
- Step E: Run failure mode tests: quota exceeded path, network partition (mock 503 from runtime), fallback to smaller model variant. Verify graceful degradation message in logs and marketplace UI.
- Step F: Submit security questionnaire and provide pen-test summary.

3) Technical checklist (copy/paste for eng handoff)
- [ ] Model versions pinned and documented (e.g., rwi-gpt-13b-v1).
- [ ] Runtime-compatible kernel list and quantization profile included.
- [ ] Endpoint URL and region routing policy specified.
- [ ] Sample curl + SDK code snippet for create-session, stream-responses, and function-calling.
- [ ] Health & metrics endpoints exposed for partner monitoring (uptime, P50/P95 latencies, tokens per second).
- [ ] Audit logging enabled and sample audit record attached.
- [ ] Billing SKU defined and test invoice provided.
- [ ] Data residency requirements and VPC options documented.

4) Service principal / IAM minimal perms (example templates)
- AWS example (managed policy names to request):
  - sts:AssumeRole (to create cross-account role in partner tests), iam:ListRoles (diagnostic), logs:CreateLogGroup/PutLogEvents (for test harness), tagging:TagResources.
- Azure example:
  - Reader + Contributor on subscription for provisioning tests, Microsoft.Support/* for support ticket automation.
- Note: do NOT request full owner on customer accounts. Keep ephemeral test credentials and rotate.

5) SKU & pricing guidance (recommended patterns)
- SKU canonical form: redwood-inference.{deployment}.{model}.{tier}.{region}
  - Example: redwood-inference.hosted.rwi-gpt-13b.standard.us-east-1
- Tiering guidance: standard (SLA best-effort), enterprise (SLA-backed, reserved capacity), burst (pay-as-you-go higher per-token but no commit).
- Billing metadata to include: model_id, quantization_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_latency_ms.
- Price testing: provide a set of synthetic workloads (prompt suites) and expected unit costs on each SKU for marketplace reviewer.

6) Suggested marketplace copy variants (short + long)
- Short (one-liner): "Redwood Inference — predictable, low-latency LLM inference with flexible hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options."
- Short (developer-focused): "Ship LLM features fast — consistent API, optimized serving runtime, and per-route cost controls."
- Long (50–80 words): "Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a production-ready LLM serving platform. Use a single API to deploy across hosted, dedicated, or private environments with transparent performance profiles, intelligent batching, and built-in fallbacks to ensure availability. Ideal for product teams that need predictable latency, cost controls, and enterprise-grade compliance."
- Call-to-action variants: "Start free trial", "Request a dedicated capacity demo", "Contact sales for private deployment".

7) QA test matrix (examples to run before go-live)
- Functional: API auth, generate, embeddings, streaming, function-calling.
- Performance: P50/P95/Tail latencies under expected load, throughput at target concurrent sessions.
- Resilience: graceful fallback to smaller model, retry/backoff behavior, circuit breaker triggers.
- Billing: synthetic transactions produce invoiceable events, SKU-mapped metadata present.
- Security: pen test summary, data exfiltration checks, KMS key usage logs.

8) UI / listing metadata to prepare
- Headline (<= 80 chars), Short description (<= 200 chars), Full description (<= 1000 chars), Tag list (AI, MLOps, Inference, Embeddings), Support URL, Documentation URL, Legal/Privacy URL.
- Recommended headline example: "High-throughput, production LLM inference for engineers."

9) Monitoring & SLOs to publish to partner (minimum)
- Uptime: 99.9% monthly (hosted).
- Latency: P95 < 1s for short prompts (<256 tokens) target region.
- Error budget: define allowed 5xx per million requests.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latencies, queue/backlog depth metric.

10) Packaging & listing artifacts (upload checklist)
- [ ] Logos (SVG + PNG).
- [ ] 3 screenshots (dashboard, onboarding, SDK example).
- [ ] Technical spec PDF.
- [ ] Support contact and escalation matrix.
- [ ] Test credentials for marketplace QA (ephemeral).
- [ ] Billing test files (sample invoice).

11) Marketing copy style notes (for UX/Content)
- Avoid deep research-speak; highlight operational guarantees and cost levers.
- Call out unique differentiators briefly: "unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private", "cost controls (batching, caching, quantization)", "rollouts and automatic fallbacks".

12) Known risks & mitigations
- Risk: Marketplace quota tests trigger autoscale that affects shared pools. Mitigation: run quota tests in dedicated sandbox or reserved capacity.
- Risk: Billing metadata mismatch causes invoice failures. Mitigation: verify SKU mapping with finance and run end-to-end invoice test.
- Risk: Listing review flags on compliance. Mitigation: pre-submit checklist to partner compliance and include required certificates.

Action items (owners & near-term next steps):
- Maya: finalize tech spec PDF and update architecture diagram (due 2024-03-08).
- Asha: export logos and screenshots in required sizes (due 2024-03-06).
- Liam: create sandbox credentials for AWS marketplace QA and share rotation plan (due 2024-03-07).
- Sofia: draft final marketplace short/long descriptions and CTA variants, run through legal copycheck (due 2024-03-09).

Open questions for partner onboarding call:
- Do partners require a demo tenant that mirrors production capacity?
- Any additional tagging taxonomy required by their billing ingestion?
- Are there timeout or request-size limits we need to surface to customers per their marketplace docs?

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider creating a small test harness repo (marketplace-test-harness) that runs the standardised prompt suite and emits a compliance report. Could be used by partners during review.
- Keep the SKU naming stable across clouds so internal billing tools can normalize usages.

End of workbook.

Revision history:
- 2024-02-12 initial draft (Maya)
- 2024-02-21 added SKU guidance and service principal perms (Liam)
- 2024-03-05 updated action items after partner sync (Asha)
